summary: Govind Swamirao Gai was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India and Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), succeeding Dineschandra Sircar.

Govind Vinayak Devasthali was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. His career included posts as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts and RYK Science College and Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Govind Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist who held the Sanskrit chair at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, succeeding Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar.
Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who served as a Professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and later as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Grace S. Fong is a Sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She served as Professor at Smith College before becoming associate professor and chair of East Asian Studies at McGill University around 1992.

Graeme MacQueen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as a lecturer at McMaster University from circa 1977 to 2003.

Grafton Elliot Smith was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the University of Sydney, Sydney Medical School, and St John's College. He held a post at University College London from circa 1919 to 1936.
Graham E. Clarke was a Tibetologist who held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford.
Graham Lock is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes is a philosopher and Japanologist who earned his Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi and later held multiple professorial and administrative chairs at University College Cork.

Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge and earned his PhD under John Lane Bell at LSE. He held major posts at Melbourne, St Andrews, and the Graduate Center, CUNY.

Graves Chamney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist educated at Fort William College. He co-founded the Royal Asiatic Society, served as its secretary, and was Professor at the East India Company College from 1819 to 1827.
Gray Tuttle is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University. He was appointed Associate Professor at Columbia University.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was an Italian linguist and Indologist. He founded the Archivio glottologico italiano in 1873 and served as Professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.
Greg Bailey is an Indologist who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He served as a professor at La Trobe University.

Gregor Ahn is a religious studies scholar who studied at Bonn and Copenhagen under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. He taught at Münster and Tartu before serving as Professor of Comparative Religion at Heidelberg University from 1996 to 2025.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, alongside receiving traditional Buddhist training.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford, supervised by Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist visual culture who studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University. He became an Associate Professor of History of Art at UC Berkeley around 1997.

Gregory Price Grieve is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.
